findings.title: Cascade-scope SKILL.md inclusion is self-contradictory and the new umbrella category isn't defined in the requirement body
findings.recommendation: Pick one of three resolutions: (a) drop the `.claude/skills/openspec-foo/SKILL.md` example from the WHEN clause AND remove the NOTE entirely → SKILL.md files default to OUT of scope (clean); (b) add `.claude/skills/<skill>/SKILL.md` as an explicit IN entry in the requirement body's `**IN — project-level governing docs**` list and remove from the WHEN's non-markdown examples → SKILL.md always IN scope; (c) add a fourth explicit category to the IN list (`**IN — orbit skill files**: `.claude/skills/<skill>/SKILL.md`, `.claude/commands/<verb>.md` per the project-level-skill umbrella`) and remove the case-by-case NOTE language → SKILL.md and command files always IN. Path (a) is the simplest and matches the design.md D7 'tight default scope' framing; later expansion can be a follow-up change.

findings.title: Producer field shape (`recommendation_options: [{label, body}]`) and consumer audit-log shape (`options_presented: ["A: …"]`) differ without an explicit transform spec
findings.recommendation: Pick one: (a) make audit-log preserve the structured shape — `options_presented: [{label, body}]` (consistent with producer; readers parse the same object); (b) document the producer→audit-log transform explicitly in the Resolution-log-shape requirement body (e.g., 'each entry in options_presented is formatted as `<label>: <body>` to give log-readers a single readable string per option'). Option (a) is cleaner; option (b) keeps the audit log scan-friendly. Either resolves the silent-transform ambiguity.

findings.title: v1 → v2 resolution-log migration claim conflates top-level aggregate with per-resolution split (loses attribution)
findings.recommendation: Rephrase the backward-compatibility paragraph to acknowledge the structural difference: v1's top-level `ripple_flagged_files_aggregate` was a flat array of strings across ALL resolutions (no per-resolution attribution); v2's per-resolution `ripple_cascade.applied / flagged_not_applied` captures attribution at the resolution level. The migration is NOT bijective — v1 archived JSONs cannot be losslessly upconverted. Add explicit reader guidance: 'consumers reading both versions should treat v1's aggregate as the union of all per-resolution ripple sets (attribution lost); v2's per-resolution form is canonical going forward.' Verified by inspecting `openspec/changes/archive/2026-05-24-lean-overlay-and-add-orbit-onboard/.orbit-runs/address-reviews-2026-05-23T18-03-25Z.json:59-66` which shows v1's top-level array shape.

findings.title: No spec scenario for malformed `recommendation_options` array (e.g., single-entry, empty, or missing label field)
findings.recommendation: Add a scenario under `Disjunctive recommendation fields surface as decision forks`: WHEN a finding's `recommendation_options` array is present but malformed (zero entries, one entry, missing `label` or `body` on an entry) THEN the consumer SHALL log a warning to stderr and fall back to heuristic detection over the `recommendation` string. This catches producer-side bugs without breaking the walk.

findings.title: Tasks group 4 (producer-side affordance) should precede group 3 (consumer-side detection) for clean reviewer-walk
findings.recommendation: Swap groups 3 and 4 (or rename them) so the producer-side `recommendation_options[]` documentation lands BEFORE the consumer-side detection logic. Reviewers reading the applied state will trace producer → consumer naturally; currently group 3 documents reading a field that group 4 then documents writing. The chunk preamble in tasks.md would shift to `Chunk 2 (groups 3-4): Producer-side affordance + consumer-side detection`. Low-priority — apply ordering doesn't actually create blocks since both groups touch independent files.

findings.title: Chunk 4 mixes AI-doable docs (group 7) with user-validation handoff (group 8); consider splitting into Chunk 4 + Chunk 5
findings.recommendation: Split the preamble: `Chunk 4 (groups 7): Documentation surface` + `Chunk 5 (groups 8): User-validation handoff`. Per `orbit-run-summary-emit`'s `Apply per-chunk-end emission` requirement, the current bundling is valid (final chunk emits with `chunk_complete: true` + `user_validation_remaining > 0`), but separating user-validation into its own chunk makes the audit trail clearer — `chunk_complete: true` at end of Chunk 4 (group 7) is unambiguously AI-done; Chunk 5 boundary cleanly marks 'awaiting user runtime validation.' Marginal ergonomic improvement.

findings.title: No spec scenario for malformed `recommendation_options` from PRODUCER side (e.g., emit a 1-entry array)
findings.recommendation: Add a scenario for producer-side enforcement: WHEN a pass attempts to emit a finding with `recommendation_options` containing fewer than 2 entries THEN the producer SHALL either (a) omit the field entirely OR (b) fail validation. This complements consumer-side S1 and prevents corrupt JSON from being emitted in the first place. Apply equivalently to orbit-audit-drift.
